hero.headline: Trump Administration Declines to Request Renewal of North American Trade Agreement
hero.body:
The Trump administration announced Wednesday it would not immediately seek to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, leaving American businesses in uncertainty about the future of the North American trade pact. The decision marks a significant shift in trade policy that affects the trilateral agreement governing commerce between the three nations.

The USMCA replaced the North American Free Trade Agreement in 2020 and has governed trade flows worth hundreds of billions of dollars annually between the United States, Mexico, and Canada. The agreement covers everything from agricultural products to automotive manufacturing to digital commerce, affecting supply chains across the continent.

The administration's decision not to pursue immediate renewal creates uncertainty for companies that have built cross-border operations around the agreement's terms. Businesses that rely on integrated supply chains spanning multiple countries now face questions about tariffs, regulations, and market access that the trade deal had previously settled.

The USMCA includes a sunset provision requiring the parties to review and potentially extend the agreement at regular intervals. The administration's announcement did not clarify whether it plans to renegotiate the agreement's terms, allow it to expire, or simply delay the renewal process. Trade experts note that prolonged uncertainty about the agreement's status could affect investment decisions and business planning across North America.

The announcement comes as businesses prepare for the second half of 2026 and make decisions about where to locate facilities and how to structure their operations. Companies in sectors heavily dependent on cross-border trade, including automotive manufacturers, agricultural exporters, and technology firms, may need to develop contingency plans if the agreement's future remains unclear.

cards.headline: Ship Traffic Resumes in Strait of Hormuz as US and Iran Hold Talks in Qatar
cards.teaser: Negotiators are meeting in Qatar for indirect talks between the United States and Iran, with ship traffic increasing in the Strait of Hormuz despite ongoing tensions.
cards.body:
Ship traffic has increased in the Strait of Hormuz following the outbreak of indirect talks between the United States and Iran in Qatar. The negotiations come after recent military exchanges between the two countries as both sides attempt to ease tensions in this critical waterway.

President Trump characterized the meetings as "very good." However, significant gaps remain between Washington and Tehran on major issues including maritime security and toll disputes. Negotiators continue working to find common ground despite the substantial differences dividing the two nations.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Chair says inflation risks declining after US-Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Kevin Warsh suggested inflation numbers are falling, pointing to substantially lower energy rates.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh addressed concerns about rising inflation Wednesday, suggesting the numbers are declining. Speaking during a panel with other central bankers at a conference in Portugal, Warsh said inflation risks have come down.

Warsh pointed to energy rates, which he said have dropped substantially since the US and Iran signed a framework agreement last month. He offered no indication about the Federal Reserve's upcoming rate decision.

cards.headline: White House considers blocking pregnant foreign nationals from entering US after Supreme Court loss
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is exploring options to restrict pregnant foreign women from entering the United States following a Supreme Court defeat on birthright .
cards.body:
The Trump administration is exploring ways to restrict pregnant foreign women from entering the United States following a Supreme Court ruling that upheld birthright citizenship. The decision struck down a Trump executive order that sought to deny citizenship to children born in the US to undocumented parents.

White House aides discussed several policy options in response to the defeat. The leading proposal would prevent pregnant foreign nationals from entering the country at the border and ports of entry, shifting focus from challenging the citizenship rights of children already born on US soil to blocking their births here. The administration characterized the approach as targeting "birth tourism," where foreign nationals travel to the US specifically to give birth and secure American citizenship for their children. Legal experts expect any such policy would face immediate court challenges over privacy rights and discrimination.

cards.headline: Syria Names Final Members of Post-Assad Parliament
cards.teaser: Syria's president has appointed the final 70 lawmakers to the country's new parliament, completing the legislative body established after the Assad government.
cards.body:
Syria's president has appointed the final 70 members of the country's new parliament, completing the legislative body following the fall of the Assad government. The new appointments include 15 women.

This move comes after regional electoral colleges selected lawmakers last October, choosing only six female candidates through that process. The completion of parliament represents progress in Syria's transition to new governing institutions in the post-Assad period.

cards.headline: Germany Charges Ukrainian Over Nord Stream Pipeline Explosions
cards.teaser: A Ukrainian national has been indicted in Germany for the 2022 sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines, a case that could strain relations between the two countries.
cards.body:
German authorities have formally charged a Ukrainian individual in connection with the September 2022 explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines linking Russia to Germany. The indictment represents a major development in the investigation into the underwater sabotage.

Ukraine denies involvement in the pipeline attacks. The case threatens to strain relations between Germany and Ukraine, which have maintained close cooperation since Russia's 2022 invasion. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy indicated that Ukraine had not yet received official information about the accusation.

cards.headline: Medicare Begins Covering Some Weight Loss Drugs for $50
cards.teaser: Medicare now covers certain GLP-1 weight loss medications at a $50 price point for eligible beneficiaries.
cards.body:
Medicare has begun covering some GLP-1 weight loss drugs at a cost of $50 for beneficiaries. The coverage represents a change in Medicare policy regarding medications in the GLP-1 class.

GLP-1 drugs have gained widespread use for weight loss in recent years. The Medicare coverage decision will make these medications more accessible to older Americans who meet eligibility requirements.

hero.headline: Venezuela Searches for Bodies and Missing After Earthquake Overwhelms Morgues
hero.body:
Venezuela is struggling to manage the aftermath of devastating back-to-back earthquakes that claimed at least 1,430 lives when they struck the country's Caribbean coast last Wednesday. The disaster has overwhelmed the nation's forensic system as bodies arrive constantly at morgues across the capital and coastal regions.

At Bello Monte mortuary in Caracas, the reality of the crisis is evident daily. "The entire street was packed with people arriving with deceased relatives," said Camila Rodríguez, a psychology student offering emotional support to grieving families. Hundreds of buildings collapsed in the quakes, Venezuela's worst earthquake event in more than 125 years, leaving tens of thousands missing and creating scenes of overwhelming tragedy.

One family's experience illustrates the scale of loss. Marjorie Cedeño lost her mother, father and brother when their four-story apartment building collapsed in Los Palos Grandes, an upmarket neighborhood. By Friday evening, she had only identified her brother through a photograph shown by forensic police. Her parents remained buried beneath the rubble, with another 25 people believed trapped in the same building.

The country's existing forensic infrastructure has been completely inadequate for the disaster's scale. Many people have transported bodies in private vehicles to Bello Monte because it is less congested than the mortuary in La Guaira, the coastal region worst affected, which has collapsed under the pressure. Edgar Hernández, former president of Venezuela's National Funeral Homes Association, said undertakers across the country have donated more than 200 coffins, body bags and other supplies to support the response.

Venezuela's acting leader, Delcy Rodríguez, announced that rescue workers had saved 33 people still alive and that an 11-year-old boy had been found alive in the town of Caraballeda. Government rescue teams have been pictured using sledgehammers and stretchers to extract dust-covered survivors from rubble.

However, on the streets there is growing anger at what many perceive as a sluggish government response. Rodríguez was heckled by frustrated locals while touring a badly affected area, with one critic shouting "The government isn't doing anything for the people!" Experts blame years of underinvestment in emergency services for the inadequate official reaction.

In contrast to the slow government response, volunteers have provided water, coffee and trauma counseling to grieving families outside mortuaries and to hundreds of families sleeping on streets because they feared returning home. Marjorie Cedeño expressed gratitude for the community effort. "There may be no government response," she said, "but there are so many good people helping."

cards.headline: Germany Charges Ukrainian Over Nord Stream Pipeline Explosions
cards.teaser: A Ukrainian national has been indicted in Germany for the 2022 sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines, a case that could strain relations between the two countries.
cards.body:
German authorities have formally charged a Ukrainian individual in connection with the September 2022 explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines linking Russia to Germany. The indictment represents a major development in the investigation into the underwater sabotage.

Ukrainian President Zelenskyy indicated that Ukraine had not yet received official information about the accusation.

cards.headline: Bombings Target Greek Government Party Members in Thessaloniki
cards.teaser: Three separate bombing attacks struck members of Greece's governing New Democracy party in the city of Thessaloniki, injuring a parliamentary candidate and others.
cards.body:
A candidate for Parliament representing Greece's governing New Democracy party was injured in one of three coordinated bombing attacks in Thessaloniki. The candidate's parents were also wounded in the attack, according to police. The bombings involved petrol bombs and other improvised devices.

The attacks occurred in the early hours and targeted multiple locations associated with the governing party. In a separate but related incident, the mother of a Greek politician died from wounds sustained in an arson attack. The series of bombings represents a significant escalation of violence against political figures in Greece.

cards.headline: Trial Begins for Businessman Accused in Maltese Journalist's Murder
cards.teaser: Yorgen Fenech is on trial for the 2017 assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, who was killed by a car bomb in Malta.
cards.body:
A Maltese businessman has gone on trial for the murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, who was killed in a car bomb explosion in October 2017. Yorgen Fenech denies any involvement in the assassination of the investigative reporter.

Caruana Galizia was a prominent investigative journalist whose work exposed corruption in Malta. Her murder drew international attention and sparked protests calling for justice and accountability. The trial represents a significant moment in Malta's efforts to address the killing and the broader issues of press freedom and corruption the case exposed.

cards.headline: Man Convicted of Attempted Murder in Dublin Attack on Three Children
cards.teaser: Riad Bouchaker has been found guilty of attempting to murder three children and assaulting four others in an attack in Dublin in November 2023.
cards.body:
A jury found Riad Bouchaker, 52, guilty of attempting to murder three children during a stabbing attack in Dublin on November 23, 2023. The violent incident horrified Ireland and sparked riots in the capital.

In addition to the attempted murder convictions, Bouchaker was found guilty of assault causing serious harm to childcare worker Leanne Flynn, and of assaulting two other children and a teenager during the same attack.

cards.headline: Syria Names Final Members of Post-Assad Parliament
cards.teaser: Syria's president has appointed the final 70 lawmakers to the country's new parliament, completing the legislative body established after the Assad government.
cards.body:
Syria's president has appointed the final 70 members of the country's new parliament, completing the legislative body following the fall of the Assad government. The new appointments include 15 women.

This move comes after regional electoral colleges selected lawmakers last October, choosing only six female candidates through that process. The completion of parliament represents progress in Syria's transition to new governing institutions in the post-Assad period.

cards.headline: Archaeologists Discover Unlooted Maya Site in Remote Mexican Forest
cards.teaser: Researchers have found intact Maya ruins in a remote area of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, naming the site Minanb after the difficulty of reaching it.
cards.body:
Archaeologists have discovered Maya monument ruins in an extremely remote location on Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula. The team drove ATVs for miles and then hiked additional miles through dense forest to reach the site, which had not been touched by looters.

The scientists named the site Minanb, a word meaning "there is no path" in reference to the extreme difficulty of accessing the location. The remote nature of the site likely contributed to its preservation, as looters have not been able to reach the monuments. The discovery provides researchers with a rare opportunity to study intact Maya structures.

hero.headline: 16 children rescued from rural Ohio home, four adults arrested
hero.body:
Law enforcement rescued 16 children from a home in rural southeastern Ohio where they were found living in squalor. Four adults, including parents and grandparents, have been arrested and charged in connection with the case. Authorities described the conditions as deplorable, with one official calling the situation "pure evil."

The children, all members of the same family, were discovered during an investigation into the property. Officials have not disclosed the specific charges filed against the four adults in custody. The rescue operation took place in a rural area of southeastern Ohio, though the exact location has not been publicly identified.

Child protective services took custody of all 16 children following their removal from the home. The investigation into the living conditions and the circumstances that led to the children being placed in this environment remains ongoing. Law enforcement agencies coordinated the rescue effort that resulted in the children being safely removed from the property.

Multiple news outlets have reported on the case, with authorities emphasizing the severity of the conditions in which the children were found. The ages of the children and the specific family relationships among all four arrested adults have not been detailed in initial reports. The case has drawn attention across Ohio and neighboring states as investigators work to determine the full scope of the situation.

The arrests mark the beginning of what is expected to be a lengthy legal process as prosecutors build cases against the four adults. Child welfare officials will now work to determine appropriate placements for the 16 children while the criminal investigation proceeds. Authorities have indicated that additional information will be released as the investigation continues and formal charges are processed through the court system.

cards.headline: Two arrested after climbing Empire State Building spire in apparent engagement stunt
cards.teaser: Two people scaled to the top of the Empire State Building's 1,454-foot spire, displayed a banner, and were taken into custody.
cards.body:
Two people were arrested Wednesday after climbing to the top of the Empire State Building's spire in New York City. The pair, dressed in black and appearing to be masked, remained atop the 1,454-foot landmark for at least ten minutes before descending.

During their time at the pinnacle, they unfurled a large black banner displaying the message: "When the power of love beats the love of power the world knows peace." The unauthorized climb appeared to be part of a marriage proposal stunt.

cards.headline: Trump to visit Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in North Dakota
cards.teaser: President Trump will visit the newly built Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in North Dakota's Badlands.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump plans to visit the newly built Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library located in North Dakota's Badlands region. The library represents a recent addition to presidential historic sites, situated in the rugged landscape where Roosevelt spent time during his life.

Trump has expressed admiration for Theodore Roosevelt and views him as a significant figure among American presidents. The visit underscores Trump's appreciation for the 26th president and his connection to the Badlands area.

cards.headline: Americans mark 250th anniversary amid national division
cards.teaser: The United States celebrated its 250th anniversary with events across the country as historians reflect on the nation's founding story.
cards.body:
Americans celebrated their nation's 250th anniversary with festivities that highlighted both patriotic pride and underlying divisions. The milestone prompted reflection on the country's founding principles and their contemporary relevance as Americans grapple with differing perspectives on the nation's past and future.

Historians have seized on the occasion to encourage Americans to revisit their founding story. The 250th anniversary has sparked broader conversations about the historical significance of the nation's establishment and how those original principles apply to modern America.

cards.headline: Lone star tick spreads across much of the U.S.
cards.teaser: The lone star tick, which can transmit alpha-gal syndrome causing red meat allergies, now covers much of the United States.
cards.body:
Lone star ticks are expanding their range across much of the United States. These ticks actively hunt down human hosts rather than waiting for contact. When they bite, they can transmit alpha-gal syndrome, a potentially dangerous allergy to red meat and other mammalian meat products.

Writer Burkhard Bilger explored the lone star tick and the risks of alpha-gal syndrome in an article for The New Yorker, examining how this expanding tick population is affecting American communities.

cards.headline: Trump's 2025 revenue included Bibles, perfume, and film royalties
cards.teaser: Official financial documents show President Trump earned billions from diverse sources including Bible sales and Home Alone royalties.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump's financial disclosures for 2025 reveal he earned more than $2 billion, with crypto investments accounting for over $1 billion of that total. The documents show Trump's family crypto projects were the primary driver of his substantial income growth last year.

The disclosures also highlight potential conflicts of interest, as Trump has actively pursued deregulation of the cryptocurrency industry while profiting significantly from it. The financial filings provide a detailed breakdown of the president's diverse revenue streams during his return to the White House.

cards.headline: Venezuela faces mounting needs one week after devastating earthquakes
cards.teaser: One week after back-to-back earthquakes struck Venezuela, the full extent of casualties and humanitarian needs remains unclear.
cards.body:
Two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela on June 24, seconds apart, devastating parts of a nation already struggling with multiple crises. The official death toll stands at more than 1,700 people, though tens of thousands remain missing. Relatives continue searching through streets lined with rubble and collapsed buildings, carrying photos of loved ones and pleading for help.

The disaster has compounded Venezuela's existing challenges following political upheaval earlier this year. With limited state presence evident in affected areas, the country faces significant obstacles as it attempts to rebuild and address immediate humanitarian needs in devastated regions.

cards.headline: Kroger to Acquire Giant Eagle for $1.65 Billion
cards.teaser: Kroger announced plans to purchase regional grocery chain Giant Eagle as competition intensifies in the supermarket sector.
cards.body:
Kroger will acquire Giant Eagle in a $1.65 billion deal, expanding the grocer's footprint as competition increases in the supermarket industry. The transaction represents a major consolidation move in the grocery sector.

Giant Eagle operates stores primarily in the mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions. The acquisition would add the regional chain to Kroger's portfolio of supermarket brands across the country.

cards.headline: White House Lifts Restrictions on Anthropic AI Models After Two-Week Ban
cards.teaser: The Trump administration removed export controls on Anthropic's most advanced AI models following a brief restriction period.
cards.body:
Anthropic has restored global access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models after the U.S. government lifted export controls that had blocked foreign nationals from using the systems. The restrictions, imposed over safety concerns that the models could be misused for cyberattacks, remained in place for more than two weeks.

U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced the decision, stating that the government had worked closely with Anthropic during the blackout period to analyze and approve Fable 5. The reversal allows the San Francisco company to resume worldwide distribution of its most advanced AI systems.

cards.headline: Micron to Donate $250 Million to Trump Investment Accounts
cards.teaser: President Trump announced that chip maker Micron would contribute to a new type of investment account for children created by his administration.
cards.body:
Micron will donate $250 million to investment accounts established by the Trump administration for children, according to the president. Trump described the contribution from the chip maker as significant for the new account program.

The administration recently created the investment account structure, though details about how the accounts operate remain limited. Trump announced the planned donation from Micron on Wednesday.

cards.headline: Multiple States Implement New Gas Taxes
cards.teaser: Several states are installing gas tax increases this week, with California's rate rising to the highest in the country.
cards.body:
California's gas tax increase takes effect Wednesday, raising the state's rate to the nation's highest. The timing aligns with the July Fourth holiday weekend, when many travelers are preparing to drive.

Multiple states are rolling out new gas taxes this week, with others planning similar increases in the coming months. The hikes will raise fuel costs for drivers across affected states during peak travel season.

cards.headline: Medicare Begins Covering Some Weight Loss Drugs for $50
cards.teaser: Medicare now covers certain GLP-1 weight loss medications at a $50 price point for eligible beneficiaries.
cards.body:
Medicare has begun covering some GLP-1 weight loss drugs at a cost of $50 for beneficiaries. The coverage represents a change in Medicare policy regarding medications in the GLP-1 class.

GLP-1 drugs have gained widespread use for weight loss in recent years. The Medicare coverage decision will make these medications more accessible to older Americans who meet eligibility requirements.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rise After Fed Chair Says Inflation Risks Declining
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Dow climbed after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh stated inflation risks have eased.
cards.body:
Stock markets advanced Wednesday following remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on inflation trends. Both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed higher after his comments. The Dow reached a fresh record to begin July, while technology stocks faced mixed results.

Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to delivering price stability, a priority he has stressed since taking office in May. He characterized inflation risks as lower than they were weeks earlier, though he stopped short of signaling the central bank's direction on interest rates for its July meeting.

hero.headline: Sony to stop producing physical game discs for new PlayStation titles in 2028
hero.body:
Sony has announced it will halt production of physical game discs for new PlayStation releases beginning in January 2028, marking a major shift toward digital-only distribution for upcoming titles.

The policy will apply exclusively to games launching after the January 2028 cutoff. Existing physical games will remain playable on current hardware, and Sony plans to continue manufacturing disc-equipped consoles to support players who want to access their existing libraries. The company confirmed the announcement through its official PlayStation blog.

The decision reflects a broader industry trend toward digital purchasing. Digital game sales have dominated PlayStation's revenue for several years, with that trend accelerating significantly during the pandemic. Sony has already offered a digital-only PlayStation 5 model since the console's launch, priced lower than the version with a disc drive.

This move will likely affect game retailers who continue stocking physical copies, though many have already reduced shelf space dedicated to games. The shift also raises concerns about game preservation and consumer rights, since digital games depend on account access and platform policies rather than physical ownership that can be resold or traded between users.

The announcement comes as Microsoft pursues similar strategies for Xbox. The company is testing a disc-to-digital program that would allow players to convert physical game collections into digital libraries. Industry reports suggest the next generation of both PlayStation and Xbox consoles may launch entirely without disc drives, completing the gaming industry's transition away from physical media.

The decline of physical game sales has been consistent over recent years as digital storefronts have become the primary purchasing method for console gamers. This shift accelerated during the pandemic when many players preferred digital downloads over in-store purchases. Sony's move essentially acknowledges this market reality by eliminating physical production for new content while grandfathering in support for existing disc-based games and hardware.

The decision does not affect games released before January 2028, which will continue to be available on physical media. Players who prefer disc-based purchasing will have until that deadline to build their physical collections. After 2028, new PlayStation game releases will only be available through digital storefronts and retailers offering digital codes.

Game preservation advocates have raised concerns about the implications of an entirely digital future, noting that games tied to online platforms can become inaccessible if companies shut down services or remove titles from digital storefronts. However, Sony's continued production of disc-equipped consoles may help mitigate some concerns for players maintaining existing libraries.

The transition represents the culmination of years of industry movement toward digital distribution, with physical media becoming increasingly marginal in the console gaming market.

cards.headline: Cloudflare mandates AI companies separate training crawlers from search or face default blocking
cards.teaser: The web infrastructure company set a September 15 deadline for AI firms to distinguish between web crawlers used for search indexing and those used for AI training.
cards.body:
Cloudflare announced a new policy requiring AI companies to separate their web crawlers used for search indexing from those used for AI model training. The company set a September 15 deadline for compliance, with non-compliant AI firms facing default blocking across many publisher sites that use Cloudflare's services.

The policy addresses publisher concerns about unauthorized content scraping for AI training. By distinguishing between search and training crawlers, publishers gain the ability to selectively permit search engine indexing while restricting access for AI training purposes. This gives content creators greater control over how their material is used by AI companies.

cards.headline: AI cloud provider Together AI raises $800 million at $8.3 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The company, which hosts open source AI models, more than doubled its valuation from the $3.3 billion it reached in early 2025.
cards.body:
Together AI secured $800 million in funding, bringing its valuation to $8.3 billion. The neocloud provider specializes in hosting open source artificial intelligence models, offering infrastructure for developers and companies building AI applications.

The funding round represents a significant jump from the company's previous $3.3 billion valuation achieved in early 2025, reflecting growing investor interest in AI infrastructure providers as demand for model hosting and deployment services accelerates across industries.

cards.headline: NASA audit casts doubt on Boeing Starliner ever achieving crew certification
cards.teaser: The space agency's inspector general indicated certification may slip to 2027, a full decade behind Boeing's original timeline.
cards.body:
A NASA inspector general report indicates Boeing's Starliner spacecraft may not receive crew certification until 2027, roughly a decade behind the company's original timeline. The assessment underscores growing concerns about the program's viability.

Boeing's Starliner has encountered multiple technical issues during testing and struggled to meet NASA's safety standards. Meanwhile, SpaceX's Dragon capsule, developed under the same Commercial Crew Program, has successfully carried astronauts to the International Space Station since 2020, widening the gap between the two competitors.

cards.headline: Microsoft tests disc-to-digital conversion feature for Xbox game libraries
cards.teaser: The program would allow players to digitize their physical game collections, as reports indicate the next Xbox console may lack a disc drive.
cards.body:
Microsoft is testing a disc-to-digital feature that would let Xbox owners convert their physical game collections into digital versions. According to sources familiar with the company's plans, this tool addresses a significant challenge as the gaming industry transitions away from physical media.

The feature comes as Microsoft prepares to release its next-generation console without a disc drive, aligning with Sony's similar shift toward all-digital hardware. Sony announced it will stop producing physical PlayStation game discs in 2028, signaling the industry-wide move away from physical media.

cards.headline: Scooter company Lime begins trading after years of financial uncertainty
cards.teaser: The bike and scooter share provider went public to help pay down approximately $1 billion in liabilities accumulated over nine years of operation.
cards.body:
Lime has become a public company after years of financial uncertainty. The nine-year-old micromobility company is using the capital from going public to address approximately $1 billion in liabilities on its balance sheet.

The scooter and bike-sharing service struggled with the challenging economics of operating in urban markets. Public market access provides Lime with the resources needed to pay down debt and continue operations as it pursues profitability.

cards.headline: Honda enters data center market with battery production for energy storage
cards.teaser: The automaker began manufacturing batteries for data centers rather than vehicles, joining the growing number of companies targeting the energy storage market.
cards.body:
Honda has begun producing batteries for data centers this week, marking a shift away from its traditional automotive focus. The move positions the automaker to capitalize on the lucrative energy storage market.

The pivot reflects the growing demand for data center infrastructure as cloud computing and artificial intelligence workloads expand. Energy storage has become increasingly valuable as companies race to build out the infrastructure needed to support these computing demands.

hero.headline: Lakers acquire Walker Kessler from Jazz in draft pick deal
hero.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have acquired center Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz in a trade centered on future draft compensation. The Lakers are sending unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 to Utah, along with first-round pick swaps in 2028 and 2030.

The trade marks a significant investment by the Lakers in the young center, who provides rim protection and rebounding. By parting with two unprotected first-round selections and two swap rights, Los Angeles has committed substantial future assets to upgrade its frontcourt.

In addition to acquiring Kessler, the Lakers are signing three players: Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, and Collin Sexton. The signings give Los Angeles additional depth and versatility across multiple positions as the team reshapes its roster.

The Jazz receive valuable draft capital that extends their collection of future picks. The unprotected nature of the 2031 and 2033 selections gives Utah potential lottery assets depending on where the Lakers stand in those seasons. The swap rights in 2028 and 2030 provide additional flexibility for Utah's front office to position itself for future draft classes.

The move represents the Lakers' focus on adding a younger core piece while maintaining veteran talent. Kessler brings defensive presence and efficiency around the basket, addressing needs that have been priorities for the organization. The accompanying signings of Mamukelashvili, Grimes, and Sexton suggest a broader roster construction strategy as Los Angeles looks to compete in the Western Conference.

cards.headline: Harry Kane surpasses Pele's World Cup goal total
cards.teaser: Kane scored against Congo DR to move past Pele on the all-time World Cup goals list.
cards.body:
Harry Kane has surpassed Pele's World Cup goals record after scoring against Congo DR in England's match. The goal moves Kane past the Brazilian legend on the all-time list for goals scored in World Cup competition.

Kane's achievement comes during the 2026 World Cup, which is being co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The England captain continues to add to his international goal tally as the tournament progresses.

cards.headline: Mitchell Robinson signs three-year deal with Celtics
cards.teaser: The center joins Boston on a $47.4 million contract after winning a championship with the Knicks.
cards.body:
Mitchell Robinson has agreed to a three-year, $47.4 million contract with the Boston Celtics, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The center comes to Boston after winning an NBA championship with the New York Knicks.

The signing bolsters the Celtics' frontcourt with a proven defender and rebounder who brings championship experience to the team.

cards.headline: Coco Gauff advances to Wimbledon third round
cards.teaser: Gauff rallied from a break down in the third set to defeat Solana Sierra in a tiebreaker.
cards.body:
Coco Gauff advanced to the third round at Wimbledon on Wednesday with a 6-3, 3-6, 7-6 (7) victory over Solana Sierra. After dropping the second set, Gauff found herself down a break in the decisive third set but mounted a comeback to force a tiebreaker.

In the tiebreaker, Gauff dominated the closing moments, winning the final six points to seal her spot in the next round. The comeback victory demonstrated her ability to perform under pressure on grass.

cards.headline: Mets owner Steve Cohen backs David Stearns
cards.teaser: Cohen said he is not considering dismissing the president of baseball operations despite consecutive disappointing seasons.
cards.body:
New York Mets owner Steve Cohen ruled out firing president of baseball operations David Stearns on Wednesday, saying "not gonna do it." The declaration came despite the team posting a second consecutive disappointing season.

Stearns is in the third year of his five-year contract with the Mets. Cohen's firm public backing of his baseball operations leader comes as the organization faces ongoing scrutiny over its recent performance and front office decisions.

cards.headline: Nationals pitcher Cade Cavalli apologizes for remark
cards.teaser: Cavalli apologized for shouting at Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras during a benches-clearing incident.
cards.body:
Washington Nationals pitcher Cade Cavalli apologized for shouting "sit down, boy" at Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras during a game. The remark came as Cavalli was involved in instigating a benches-clearing scrum between the two teams.

Cavalli stated he meant no ill will with the comment. The incident sparked a confrontation that cleared both benches onto the field during the interleague matchup.

cards.headline: England penalty decision reviewed under VAR protocol
cards.teaser: Officials review major incidents including a potential foul on an England player during World Cup play.
cards.body:
Video assistant referee protocol is being examined following a penalty decision involving England during World Cup competition. The review focuses on a potential foul on an England player and whether the decision to award a penalty was correctly applied under the laws of the game.

VAR has been used throughout the tournament to review major incidents and provide additional oversight on key decisions. The system allows match officials to examine video footage of potential penalties, red cards, and other significant moments to ensure accurate application of the rules.

hero.headline: Danny Glover Reveals Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis
hero.body:
Actor Danny Glover has announced that he has been living with Alzheimer's disease for several years. The 79-year-old shared the news during an interview on The Today Show, revealing that he received his diagnosis not long after being honored with an honorary Oscar in 2022.

During the interview, Glover discussed how he is managing the condition. "I could live with it, in a sense. I'm sure as it advances, things are going to be different and changing," he explained. He noted that his movements, speech, and memory have already begun to slow as the disease progresses. Despite these challenges, Glover emphasized that he does not view his diagnosis as the end of his life, stating that there is still work to be done and his life continues.

Glover's family has been instrumental in his support throughout this time. He credited them for having his back as he navigates living with the disease.

Glover's career has spanned more than four decades in film and television. He gained widespread recognition for his role as Roger Murtaugh in the Lethal Weapon film series alongside Mel Gibson. His extensive filmography also includes acclaimed performances in The Color Purple and Beloved, as well as the recently concluded television series Station Eleven. Beyond his work as an actor, Glover has maintained a long-standing commitment to humanitarian causes and social activism.

Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurological condition that affects memory, thinking, and behavior. It stands as the most common form of dementia among older adults. The disease typically worsens gradually, though the pace of progression varies considerably from person to person. In its early stages, individuals often experience difficulty recalling recent events or conversations. As the disease advances, symptoms can include severe memory loss and increasing difficulty performing everyday activities.

Glover's public announcement reflects a broader trend of prominent figures sharing their Alzheimer's diagnoses. Former President Ronald Reagan announced his diagnosis in 1994, bringing significant public attention to the disease. More recently, musician Tony Bennett lived publicly with his diagnosis following his diagnosis in 2016 until his death in 2023. Actor Chris Hemsworth also disclosed in 2022 that genetic testing revealed an increased risk of developing the disease, prompting him to pause his acting career.

The medical landscape for Alzheimer's treatment has evolved in recent years, with the FDA approving new treatments designed to slow disease progression. However, questions remain about access to these treatments and their long-term effectiveness. Current estimates suggest that more than six million Americans are living with Alzheimer's disease, with projections indicating this number will continue to rise as the population ages.

cards.headline: Netflix Acquires JonBenét Ramsey Murder Limited Series From Paramount+
cards.teaser: The scripted series about the 1996 murder case moves to Netflix, with a premiere set for this winter.
cards.body:
Netflix has acquired the scripted limited series about the murder of JonBenét Ramsey from Paramount+. The streaming service will release the series this winter, with a specific premiere date to be announced. The show is now titled The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey.

The series stars Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen in leading roles. The six-year-old beauty pageant contestant was found dead in her family's Boulder, Colorado home in December 1996. The case remains one of the most publicized unsolved murders in American history, spawning numerous documentaries and investigations over the past three decades.

cards.headline: Trump Received $10.7 Million for Amazon Documentary About First Lady
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump reported a licensing fee from Amazon MGM Studios for the documentary Melania as part of his 2025 financial disclosure.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump reported a $10.71 million licensing fee as income in his 2025 financial disclosure report for Melania, an Amazon MGM Studios documentary about First Lady Melania Trump. Amazon MGM Studios acquired the documentary for $40 million and spent $35 million on marketing.

Financial disclosure reports are required of federal officials to provide transparency about potential conflicts of interest and income sources. The payment represents a significant entertainment-related transaction in Trump's latest filing.

cards.headline: Camp Rock 3 Gets August Release Date on Disney Channel
cards.teaser: Disney released a teaser for the franchise reboot, with the Jonas Brothers and Demi Lovato returning as executive producers.
cards.body:
Disney unveiled a teaser for Camp Rock 3, rebooting the franchise that launched the careers of the Jonas Brothers and Demi Lovato. The film will premiere on August 13 on Disney Channel and the following day on Disney+. The teaser introduces new campers and music for the reboot.

The Jonas Brothers and Lovato return as executive producers on the project, with the brothers also reprising their roles from the original films. The first Camp Rock premiered in 2008 on Disney Channel, becoming one of the network's most-watched original movies. A sequel, Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam, followed in 2010.

cards.headline: Russian Rooftoppers Climb Empire State Building in Apparent Engagement
cards.teaser: Ivan Beerkus and Angela Nikolau, stars of the Netflix documentary Skywalkers, illegally scaled the New York skyscraper.
cards.body:
Two people in black clothing scaled the Empire State Building without authorization on Wednesday and reached the building's spire, well above the public observation areas. They unfurled a large black banner displaying the message: "When the power of love beats the love of power the world knows peace." The pair spent at least ten minutes at the top before descending.

Both climbers were arrested following the stunt. The couple has been identified as Ivan Beerkus and Angela Nikolau, Russian rooftoppers featured in Netflix's 2024 documentary Skywalkers: A Love Story, which chronicled their climbs of tall structures worldwide without safety equipment.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Wins Rights to Siren Head Movie Based on Internet Legend
cards.teaser: The studio prevailed in a bidding war for the Gen Z horror phenomenon created by artist Trevor Henderson.
cards.body:
Warner Bros. has acquired the rights to Siren Head after winning a bidding war for the property. Brian Duffield will direct the film, with Zach Cregger, director of Weapons, co-writing the screenplay. The project follows the recent success of Backrooms, another internet-born horror property adapted for film.

Siren Head was created by artist Trevor Henderson and became a viral internet sensation. The urban legend centers on a mysterious predator characterized by two sirens. The character has become popular among Gen Z audiences through social media and online horror communities, spawning fan art, stories, and video game adaptations.

cards.headline: Fox Releases First Footage of Baywatch Reboot
cards.teaser: A new teaser trailer shows the lifeguard team in action, with the series bringing back the iconic beach patrol concept.
cards.body:
Fox unveiled the first footage from its Baywatch reboot in a new teaser trailer. The trailer features characters Hobie Buchannon, played by Stephen Amell, Charlie Vale, played by Jessica Belkin, and Luke, played by Noah Beck, running and leaping across the sand. Character Nat, played by Hassie Harrison, declares it the best job in the world.

The original Baywatch series ran from 1989 to 2001 and became one of the most-watched television shows globally. The series followed lifeguards patrolling the beaches of Los Angeles County, California. A feature film adaptation starring Dwayne Johnson was released in 2017.

hero.headline: Former CIA Director John Brennan sues Justice Department over ongoing investigation
hero.teaser: John Brennan filed suit demanding the Justice Department preserve all records related to its investigation into him.
hero.body:
Former CIA Director John Brennan filed suit Wednesday demanding the Justice Department preserve all records related to its ongoing investigation, saying the materials will be needed to defend himself against what he calls a vindictive prosecution. The suit represents Brennan's first formal legal action after months under investigation in Florida.

Brennan characterized the Justice Department probe as phantom criminal conduct. The former intelligence chief has been under investigation as part of an inquiry whose specific focus has not been publicly detailed.

cards.headline: White House considers blocking pregnant foreign nationals from entering US after Supreme Court loss
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is exploring options to restrict pregnant foreign women from entering the United States following a Supreme Court defeat on birthright .
cards.body:
The Trump administration is exploring ways to restrict pregnant foreign women from entering the United States following a Supreme Court ruling that upheld birthright citizenship. The decision struck down a Trump executive order that sought to deny citizenship to children born in the US to undocumented parents.

White House aides discussed several policy options in response to the defeat. The leading proposal would prevent pregnant foreign nationals from entering the country at the border and ports of entry, shifting focus from challenging the citizenship rights of children already born on US soil to blocking their births here. The administration characterized the approach as targeting "birth tourism," where foreign nationals travel to the US specifically to give birth and secure American citizenship for their children. Legal experts expect any such policy would face immediate court challenges over privacy rights and discrimination.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Chair says inflation risks declining after US-Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Kevin Warsh suggested inflation numbers are falling, pointing to substantially lower energy rates.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh addressed concerns about rising inflation Wednesday, suggesting the numbers are declining. Speaking during a panel with other central bankers at a conference in Portugal, Warsh said inflation risks have come down.

Warsh pointed to energy rates, which he said have dropped substantially since the US and Iran signed a framework agreement last month. He offered no indication about the Federal Reserve's upcoming rate decision.

cards.headline: Democrats accuse Trump of improper profit from cryptocurrency ventures
cards.teaser: President Trump reported more than $1 billion in income tied to cryptocurrency in his annual financial disclosure.
cards.body:
Democrats accused President Trump of improperly profiting from his family's cryptocurrency ventures after he reported more than $1 billion in income tied to the industry. Trump's annual financial disclosure released Tuesday showed approximately $594 million in income from World Liberty Financial, the crypto business he launched with his sons.

The disclosure covers income from multiple cryptocurrency-related activities. Democrats argue the president is using his office to enrich himself through the digital currency industry.

cards.headline: House Republicans stall own agenda over SAVE America Act for second week
cards.teaser: GOP infighting has left President Trump's SAVE America Act in limbo.
cards.body:
House Republicans ground their own agenda to a halt for the second consecutive week over President Trump's SAVE America Act. Internal GOP divisions have prevented progress on the legislation, leaving the bill in limbo despite party control of the chamber.

The stalemate represents a setback for the Trump administration's legislative priorities. Republican leadership has been unable to unify the caucus around the measure.

cards.headline: Navy helicopter crew member missing after emergency landing in Arabian Sea
cards.teaser: An MH-60S Seahawk made an emergency water landing Wednesday morning with four aircrewmen aboard.
cards.body:
A Navy helicopter assigned to a US aircraft carrier made an emergency water landing in the Arabian Sea Wednesday morning, and one of the four aircrewmen is missing. The MH-60S Seahawk, a twin engine helicopter, went down in the water according to the US military.

The Seahawk can be used for search and rescue, special operations, combat support, and other missions. Search efforts for the missing crew member are ongoing.

cards.headline: Trump administration criticizes Venezuelan opposition leader over return attempts
cards.teaser: Maria Corina Machado's efforts to return to Venezuela after earthquakes drew criticism from State Department officials.
cards.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado's repeated attempts to return to her home country after devastating earthquakes last week angered Trump administration officials. Multiple senior administration officials said Machado's high-profile return efforts created extra needless drama for the State Department and threatened to inflame political tensions in Venezuela during US-assisted relief efforts.

A senior administration official called Machado's actions political opportunism and grotesque. Four other officials echoed similar sentiments about the opposition leader's attempts to return during the humanitarian crisis.
